extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals; PRSA members; general public interested in PR accreditation
extracted.subtask_description: A 1965 press announcement listing 430 public relations executives accredited by the Public Relations Society of America and describing the Society's accreditation program and requirements. Useful for extracting accreditation criteria and procedural details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the accreditation program
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘The purpose of the accreditation program is to raise the professional standards of public relations and to recognize those who have demonstrated a high level of competence in the public relations field.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains the program's goal to improve professional standards and to confer recognition on individuals meeting those standards. (Verbatim phrasing from the announcement.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination structure (two-part examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘The Society's accreditation program ... comprises a two-part examination. The written examination is given under the supervision of a professional testing firm. Oral examinations are conducted by a three-man team of examiners, all of whom are themselves accredited.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that accreditation requires passing both a written exam (administered under professional testing supervision) and an oral exam (conducted by a three-member panel of accredited examiners).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-exam eligibility standards: experience, character, reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘An applicant for accreditation must pass the two examinations and, also meet other rigid standards of experience, character and reputation before the Accreditation board approves and grants PRSA accreditation.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that passing exams alone is insufficient: applicants must also satisfy strict, board-reviewed standards regarding professional experience, personal character, and reputation prior to acceptance.
